knowledgeAnswers.rationale: WorkSafe Victoria says powdered bleach containing persulphate salts can irritate the eyes and nose, and that a small quantity of dust is enough to irritate.
The label sets the processing time. The booking is moved, not the processing time, and any change is recorded as an incident.
According to Safe Work Australia, from 1 December 2026 the WEL schedule takes over from the WES schedule. State adoption is to be checked.

practicalCriteria: Assessor observes the candidate read the label and the safety data sheet, and state the processing time, before mixing any product
Assessor observes the candidate mix a colour to the label ratio and label the mixed product with name, date and dilution
Assessor observes the candidate use gloves and eye protection suited to the product, and keep the mixing area clear of food and drink
Assessor checks that the candidate states which hazards apply to PPD, peroxide and powdered bleach, using the WorkSafe Victoria list
passRule: 80% on knowledge checks; practical sign-off separate
evidenceRequired: Photo of the label and the safety data sheet for each product used in the simulation
Record of the mix, the processing time and any reaction
Written answer to the hazard question, using the WorkSafe list
stopWorkCriteria: Dust is visible from powdered bleach and the candidate continues without closing the container
The candidate changes a processing time to fit the schedule
An aerosol colour is about to be used on eyebrows or eyelashes
A product has no label or no safety data sheet on hand
